extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examining/processing staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, document requirements, and quality standards governing how provisional and nonprovisional U.S. patent applications are received, accorded a filing date, processed by the Office of Initial Patent Examination (OIPE), and how misplaced/unmatched/unlocatable papers are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components necessary for filing date for nonprovisional applications (37 CFR 1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The component parts of a nonprovisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) necessary to obtain a filing date are: a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 and 37 CFR 1.71; a claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 and 37 CFR 1.75; and a drawing, if necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 (first sentence) and 37 CFR 1.81(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted papers are too informal to be given a filing date (e.g., specification is obviously informal or incoherent), the case is held as incomplete and no filing date is granted until corrections are made; the filing date will be the date the corrections are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and handling of incomplete nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If nonprovisional application papers filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) do not include required parts or are too informal, OIPE prepares and mails a Notice of Incomplete Application and holds the case as incomplete; no filing date is granted until the incompleteness is corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of incompleteness include omission of specification, omission of at least one claim (for nonprovisional), or missing drawings if required. Applicants are informed of shortcomings and must correct them to obtain a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of nonprovisional applications filed without all inventors/names/fees/oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing dates are accorded to nonprovisional applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) even if submitted without the names of all inventors, required fees (basic filing fee, search and examination fees), and/or the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIPE mails a notice requiring the appropriate fees and the oath/declaration (which must include names of all inventors) to be filed, accompanied by a surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)). Rules on whether the surcharge is required depend on filing date ranges (e.g., applications filed on or after certain dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application size fee is required for any application filed on or after December 8, 2004 whose specification and drawings (excluding certain electronic sequence or program listings) exceed 100 sheets of paper; the fee applies for each additional 50 sheets or fraction thereof over 100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings/computer program listings filed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e)/1.96 and in electronic medium are excluded when determining application size fee. The application size fee must be paid prior to expiration of the time period set for reply in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment (37 CFR 1.53(f)(3)). See MPEP § 607 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment limitations and fee consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) may be filed with a preliminary amendment limited to the cancellation of claims; any preliminary amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 and include a complete listing of all claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office strongly recommends filing with the desired set of claims rather than filing then cancelling claims. A preliminary amendment cancelling claims will reduce the number of claims considered in filing fee calculation. No refund will be made once the fee for claims is properly paid even if claims are later cancelled, unless a petition for express abandonment under 37 CFR 1.138(d) is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of provisional application subsequent to filing (cover sheet, fee, surcharge, correspondence address rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional application accorded a filing date does not include the cover sheet required by § 1.51(c)(1) or the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(d)), applicant will be notified and given a period to pay the basic filing fee, file the cover sheet, and pay the surcharge required by § 1.16(g) to avoid abandonment (if a correspondence address § 1.33(a) was provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no correspondence address was provided, applicant has two months from the filing date to complete these items. If the application size fee (1.16(s)) is not paid on filing, it must be paid prior to expiration of the time set for reply in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of provisional applications (no examination and 12-month abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application for a patent filed under paragraph (c) will not be placed on the files for examination and will become abandoned no later than twelve months after its filing date pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment other than to make the provisional comply with statute and regulations may be made to a provisional application after its filing date (see 37 CFR 1.53(c)). A provisional that lacks a cover sheet may be treated as a nonprovisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date definition and review of refusal to accord filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the provisional or nonprovisional application is the date of receipt in the Office of the application which includes a specification containing description pursuant to 37 CFR 1.71 and at least one claim (required for nonprovisional applications) pursuant to 37 CFR 1.75, and any drawings required by 37 CFR 1.81(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If items are missing, applicant will be notified and filing date will be the receipt date of the missing parts. Review of a refusal to grant a filing date is by petition with petition fee (37 CFR 1.17). Petitioner should present arguments that items were not missing or that a filing date should be assigned. For properly deposited Express Mail under 37 CFR 1.10, the deposit date may be the filing date; petitions and supporting evidence should be provided to seek review. Petitions on these matters are decided in the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy (MPEP § 1002.02(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OIPE drawing review standards for initial publication scanning
rubrics_metrics.description: OIPE performs an initial review of drawings to determine if they can be effectively scanned and adequately reproduced for publication; the standard is liberal so most drawings (including informal ones) will be accepted, but OIPE may object when drawings cannot be adequately scanned or reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical drawing defects prompting objection: (A) line quality too light or illegible text (37 CFR 1.84(l), (p)(1)); (B) missing lead lines (37 CFR 1.84(q)); (C) excessive text or text not in English (37 CFR 1.84(o), (p)(2) and 1.52(d)(1)); (D) incorrect margins or paper size (37 CFR 1.84(f), (g)) — top & left margins at least 2.5 cm, right at least 1.5 cm, bottom at least 1.0 cm; (E) figures not labeled "Fig." with consecutive Arabic numerals/capital letters (37 CFR 1.84(u)(1)); (F) photographs that could be illustrated by drawings but are illegible after scanning (37 CFR 1.84(b)); (G) color drawings/color photos without a petition to accept color. If OIPE objects, applicant is notified and must file corrected drawings (usually within two months) in paper to the address in the Notice to avoid abandonment. No fee is required for corrected drawings required by OIPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal application definition and correction procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is informal if it is typed on both sides of paper, or is not permanent, legible, or reproducible. OIPE accords a filing date to papers that include a specification and at least one claim (when required) even if they do not comply with rules, and issues a Notice of Informal Application indicating the informality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If informalities are timely corrected, the application is given the filing date of the original informal papers. Failure to correct within specified time results in abandonment. The transmittal letter for continuing applications should identify any provisional or parent application information to simplify processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling papers sent to wrong Technology Center (TC) and unmatched papers
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings, amendments, or other papers are delivered to the wrong TC, the correct TC assignment should be obtained from PALM, placed on the paper, and the paper forwarded to the appropriate TC. Unmatched papers collections (e.g., "application number too high") should be reviewed frequently and forwarded appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a TC does not have a corresponding application, inquire of OIPE to determine TC of record; if none, send to Paper Correlating Office (PCO). For papers with application numbers, check OIPE and PALM. Papers with an examiner's name require careful TC record check and consultation. Each paper sent to PCO must have a fully completed PCO Transmittal Form; incomplete forms may cause return to originating TC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unmatched papers for files sent to Publishing Division or File Information Unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers for applications indicated by PALM to be in Publishing Division locations (7400-7650) should be forwarded to Publishing Division; papers for applications in the File Information Unit (location 9210) should be forwarded to the PCO for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers requiring examiner review will be returned to the TC after Publishing Division personnel match the paper to the file. These forwarding instructions apply also to files in issue or with assigned patent numbers and issue dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlocatable file procedure (37 CFR 1.251) and applicant compliance options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office cannot locate the file of an application, patent, or other proceeding after a reasonable search, the Office will notify the applicant or patentee and set a time period to comply under 37 CFR 1.251 by one of three options: (a)(1) provide a copy of the applicant's/patentee's correspondence record, a list of such correspondence, and a statement that the copy is complete and accurate; (a)(2) produce the record for Office copying and provide a completeness statement; or (a)(3) state that the applicant/patentee does not possess any record of correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pending applications, failure to comply within the time period set results in abandonment. The Office typically sets a three-month reply period in an application (extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a) by three months up to six months total) and a six-month reply period in a patent (not extendable). If applicant produces records for copying under (a)(2), they should be brought to the Customer Service Center in OIPE. If reply to a notice in an application is filed after three months, patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) may be reduced by the late days (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C)(ii) and 37 CFR 1.704(b)). The Office may issue a 1.251 notice when informal attempts to obtain missing documents are unsuccessful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between missing documents and unlocatable files
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.251 generally applies when the entire file cannot be located. When a document is missing from an application, Office practice is to call the applicant's representative and request submission (generally by facsimile) of a copy, rather than issuing a 1.251 notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if informal attempts fail, the Office may issue a 1.251 notice and include a printout of the PALM contents entries. Applicants must also provide any appendix or information disclosure statement submitted with the application (these are not in PACR), though U.S. patent documents can be obtained by the Office from internal databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to respond to 1.251 notice and related procedural impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with a 1.251 notice within the time period set will result in abandonment of a pending application; for patents failing to comply, the Office may take action under 37 CFR 41.128 or 37 CFR 10.18. A missing reply can affect patent term adjustment and the only certified copy of the file may be the patent and application-as-filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects include loss of enforceable file history for enforcement, possible action by the Office in ongoing proceedings, and reduction of PTA for late replies as described under 35 U.S.C. 154(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and electronic imaging (Image File Wrapper, IFW)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications filed on or after June 30, 2003 are electronically scanned and loaded into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) system; once loaded, examiners and staff perform processing and examination using IFW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling of models, exhibits, and specimens has separate procedures (see MPEP § 608.03). For IFW processing, see the IFW Manual. Effective December 1, 2003, no official paper relating to a pending application may be personally delivered to a Technology Center (with limited national security exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers received after patenting or abandonment and unmatched paper frequency review
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is patented or abandoned, incoming communications not to become part of the record will be returned to sender by the Technology Center. Collections of unmatched papers (e.g., "application number too high") should be reviewed at least once a week and handled per the appropriate routing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PALM indicates an application is in a TC but file is not available, retain papers in the TC for processing or forward to PCO as instructed. Use PALM and OIPE inquiries to determine correct routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees payable and availability of current USPTO fee schedule (37 CFR 1.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are payable in advance as governed by 37 CFR 1.22; applicants should consult the latest fee schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The latest fee schedule is available from the USPTO by phone or on the USPTO webpage. See MPEP § 607 and relevant CFR sections for fee amounts and when surcharges apply.
